title: useState declares a state variable
body: useState is a React Hook that lets you add a state variable to a component. Call const [state, setState] = useState(initialValue) at the top level of your component. React keeps the state between re-renders. The setter replaces the previous value; passing an updater function receives the pending state. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the full API reference.

title: Rules of Hooks
body: Only call Hooks at the top level of a React function component or a custom Hook. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, nested functions, or after an early return. Only call Hooks from React functions, not from regular JavaScript functions or class components. These rules let React preserve Hook state across renders in a stable order.

title: useEffect synchronizes with an external system
body: useEffect lets you synchronize a component with an external system. React runs the effect after the component commits to the screen. Return a cleanup function to undo the subscription or timer. Declare every reactive value used inside the effect in the dependency array. Effects are for external systems; you usually do not need an Effect to transform data for rendering.

title: use client marks a Client Component module
body: The 'use client' directive tells bundlers to treat the module and its imports as Client Components. Put it at the top of the file, before imports. Use it when the module uses state, effects, or browser-only APIs. Server Components are the default in React Server Components apps and do not need a directive. Client Components can import other Client Components, not Server Components.

title: Basic routing with app.METHOD
body: Routing determines how an Express app responds to a client request for a particular path and HTTP method. app.get('/path', handler) handles GET requests. The handler receives (req, res, next). Send a response with res.send, res.json, or res.end. Path patterns can include named parameters such as /users/:userId, available as req.params.userId.

title: Using middleware
body: Middleware functions have access to the request, the response, and the next function in the cycle. They can execute code, change req and res, end the cycle, or call next() to continue. Application-level middleware is bound with app.use or app.METHOD. If a middleware function does not call next() or end the response, the request hangs. Error-handling middleware takes four arguments: (err, req, res, next).

title: Error handling
body: Define error-handling middleware last, after other app.use and route calls, with four arguments: (err, req, res, next). In Express 5, rejected promises in middleware and handlers are passed to the error handler automatically. You can still call next(err) to skip to the error handler. Do not write to the response after headers have been sent.

title: safeParse vs parse
body: schema.parse(data) validates and returns the typed value, or throws a ZodError if validation fails. schema.safeParse(data) returns a discriminated result: { success: true, data } or { success: false, error }. Prefer safeParse in request handlers and agent tools so a bad payload does not throw. The error object lists issues with a path and message for each failed check.

title: z.object defines a typed object schema
body: z.object({ name: z.string(), count: z.number().int() }) describes an object and infers its TypeScript type. Unknown keys are stripped by default in many setups; use .strict() to reject them or .passthrough() to keep them. Build nested objects by composing schemas. Optional fields use .optional() or .default(value).

title: z.infer gets the TypeScript type from a schema
body: Use z.infer<typeof schema> to extract the output TypeScript type of a Zod schema. Use z.input<typeof schema> when the input type differs from the output, for example after .transform or .default. Inferring types from the schema keeps runtime validation and compile-time types in sync so you do not maintain a parallel interface.

title: App Router uses the app directory
body: The Next.js App Router is defined by files in the app/ directory. page.tsx is a route's UI, layout.tsx wraps segments and preserves state on navigation, loading.tsx and error.tsx define fallback UI, and route.ts defines a Route Handler. Folders name the URL segment. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the full App Router reference.

title: Server Actions run on the server from a form or call
body: A Server Action is an async function marked with the 'use server' directive. You can pass it to a form action or call it from a Client Component. Next.js creates a POST endpoint for the action and treats the returned data as a mutation so the router can refresh cached data. Validate arguments on the server; do not trust client input. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the full reference.

title: generateMetadata sets per-route title and Open Graph tags
body: Export generateMetadata from a page or layout to set a route's <title>, description, and Open Graph fields. The function can be async and receives the route params and searchParams. Returned fields are shallow-merged with parent layouts. Use the metadata object instead when the values are static. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the full Metadata API.

title: fs/promises is the async file API
body: import { readFile, writeFile, mkdir } from 'node:fs/promises' returns Promises instead of using callbacks. readFile(path, 'utf8') resolves to a string. writeFile overwrites by default; use the flag option to append. Paths may be strings or URL file: objects. Prefer this module over fs.promises in new ESM code. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the full Node.js API.

title: fetch is a global HTTP client in Node.js
body: Node.js provides a global fetch() that follows the WHATWG Fetch Standard, plus Request, Response, Headers, and FormData. await fetch(url) returns a Response; call response.json() or response.text() to read the body. For a POST, pass { method: 'POST', headers, body }. Undici implements this API. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the full Node.js API.

title: path.join and path.extname build portable file paths
body: import path from 'node:path'. path.join('src', 'index.ts') joins segments with the platform separator and normalizes '.' and '..'. path.extname('a.ts') returns '.ts'. path.resolve starts from the current directory unless given an absolute segment. On Windows, path.win32 and path.posix expose explicit variants. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the full Node.js API.

title: strict turns on the recommended type-checking suite
body: Setting "strict": true in tsconfig.json enables strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny, strictFunctionTypes, strictBindCallApply, strictPropertyInitialization, and useUnknownInCatchVariables. Under strictNullChecks, string | null is not assignable to string without a narrowing check. Prefer enabling strict in new projects rather than toggling flags one by one. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the TypeScript Handbook.

title: Partial, Pick, Omit, and Record are built-in utility types
body: TypeScript ships utility types that transform other types. Partial<T> makes every property optional. Required<T> makes them required. Pick<T, K> keeps a key set, Omit<T, K> drops a key set, and Record<K, T> builds an object type from keys K to values T. ReturnType<F> and Parameters<F> extract a function's return and parameter types. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the TypeScript Handbook.

title: satisfies checks a value against a type without widening it
body: The satisfies operator validates that an expression matches a type while keeping the expression's more specific inferred type. For example, const palette = { red: [255, 0, 0], green: '#00ff00' } satisfies Record<string, string | number[]> still lets you use palette.red.map because red stays a number array. Use it when as would hide mistakes or when an annotation would widen literals. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the TypeScript Handbook.

title: pathlib.Path is the object-oriented path API
body: from pathlib import Path. Path('src') / 'app.py' joins paths in a portable way. Path.read_text() and Path.write_text() handle encoding, Path.iterdir() lists a directory, Path.glob('**/*.py') searches recursively, and Path.exists() / Path.is_file() test the filesystem. Prefer Path over os.path in new code. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Python standard library docs.

title: dataclasses generate __init__ and comparison methods
body: from dataclasses import dataclass, field. @dataclass on a class synthesizes __init__, __repr__, and comparison methods from annotated fields. Use field(default_factory=list) for mutable defaults. @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) makes instances immutable and uses __slots__. keyword-only fields can be marked with kw_only=True. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Python standard library docs.

title: asyncio.run and TaskGroup drive async programs
body: asyncio.run(main()) starts an event loop, runs the coroutine, and shuts the loop down. Inside async functions, await asyncio.sleep(n) yields, and asyncio.gather(*coros) waits for many tasks. In 3.11+, async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg: tg.create_task(...) is the preferred way to run tasks and cancel the rest if one fails. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Python standard library docs.

title: Path and query parameters are declared in the function signature
body: In FastAPI, @app.get('/items/{item_id}') def read_item(item_id: int, q: str | None = None) treats item_id as a path parameter and q as an optional query parameter. Types are validated and documented in OpenAPI automatically. Use Query(), Path(), and Field() for constraints such as ge, le, min_length, and descriptions. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the FastAPI tutorial.

title: Depends injects shared dependencies into a path operation
body: Declare a parameter as dep: Annotated[Type, Depends(provider)] so FastAPI calls provider, caches the result for the request, and injects it. Common uses are database sessions, current-user auth, and shared query parameters. A dependency can itself depend on others. Yield-based dependencies can run cleanup after the response. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the FastAPI tutorial.

title: Pydantic models declare request and response bodies
body: Define a class Item(BaseModel) with typed fields and use it as a parameter (item: Item) to parse and validate the JSON request body, or as response_model to filter the response. Nested models and lists work as fields. Use model_config or Field() for examples and constraints. FastAPI generates the OpenAPI schema from the same models. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the FastAPI tutorial.

title: A Model maps a Python class to a database table
body: class Book(models.Model) with fields such as models.CharField(max_length=200), ForeignKey, and ManyToManyField defines a table. Each model has an implicit AutoField primary key named id unless you set primary_key=True. makemigrations and migrate create and apply schema changes. Meta.ordering, db_table, and unique_together (or UniqueConstraint) configure the model. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Django docs.

title: QuerySets are lazy until you evaluate them
body: Book.objects.filter(title__icontains='x').exclude(published=False) returns a QuerySet that does not hit the database until you iterate it, slice it, or call list(), count(), or exists(). Use get() for a single row (it raises DoesNotExist or MultipleObjectsReturned). select_related and prefetch_related reduce JOIN/query counts. update() and delete() act in bulk. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Django docs.

title: path() connects a URL pattern to a view
body: In urls.py, urlpatterns = [path('articles/<int:pk>/', views.article_detail, name='article-detail')] captures typed path converters and passes them as view kwargs. include() mounts another URLconf. A view is a function or class-based view (as_view()) that takes a request and returns an HttpResponse. reverse('article-detail', args=[pk]) or the {% url %} tag builds a URL from the name. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Django docs.

title: A DataFrame is a labeled two-dimensional table
body: pd.DataFrame(data, columns=..., index=...) builds a table of Series aligned on an index. df['col'] selects a column, df.loc[labels] selects by label, and df.iloc[i] selects by position. read_csv, read_parquet, and to_csv / to_parquet are the usual I/O entry points. Use assign and copy when you need a new object; many operations return a copy rather than modifying in place. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the pandas user guide.

title: groupby splits, applies, and combines
body: df.groupby('key').agg({'value': 'sum'}) splits rows by key, applies an aggregation, and combines the result with the group keys as the index. Use as_index=False to keep keys as columns. groupby also supports .sum(), .mean(), .size(), .transform() (same shape as the input), and .apply(). Passing a list of keys creates a MultiIndex. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the pandas user guide.

title: merge joins DataFrames on columns or indexes
body: pd.merge(left, right, on='id', how='inner') performs SQL-style joins. how can be 'inner', 'left', 'right', or 'outer'. Use left_on and right_on when the key names differ, and suffixes when overlapping column names need renaming. concat stacks objects along an axis; join is a convenient index-based merge on the caller. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the pandas user guide.

title: ndarray is a typed, fixed-shape N-dimensional array
body: np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]], dtype=np.float64) builds an ndarray. arr.shape, arr.dtype, and arr.ndim describe it. np.zeros, np.ones, np.arange, and np.linspace construct new arrays. Vectorized operators and ufuncs (np.sin, np.sum, np.mean) run over the whole array without Python loops. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the NumPy user guide.

title: Broadcasting aligns array shapes for elementwise ops
body: NumPy compares shapes from the trailing dimension forward. Dimensions are compatible if they are equal or one of them is 1; a missing dimension is treated as 1. So a (3, 1) array plus a (1, 4) array yields a (3, 4) result. Use arr[:, None] or np.newaxis to insert a length-1 axis. Broadcasting avoids explicit tiles and copies when it can. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the NumPy user guide.

title: Integer, slice, and boolean indexing select arrays
body: arr[0, :3] uses basic slicing and returns a view when possible. Integer array indexing and boolean masks (arr[arr > 0]) produce copies. arr[..., 0] uses an ellipsis to fill missing axes. Combine slices with np.ix_ or mesh-style indexing to take a sub-grid. Prefer views for large data when you do not need a copy. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the NumPy user guide.

title: models in schema.prisma define tables and relations
body: A Prisma model is declared in schema.prisma: model User { id String @id @default(cuid()) email String @unique posts Post[] }. Relations use typed fields plus @relation on the foreign-key side. Run prisma migrate dev to create SQL migrations and prisma generate to refresh Prisma Client. Scalar types include String, Int, Boolean, DateTime, Json, and Decimal. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Prisma docs.

title: Prisma Client findMany, create, and update are typed CRUD helpers
body: const users = await prisma.user.findMany({ where: { email: { contains: '@' } }, include: { posts: true }, orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }, take: 20 }) returns typed objects. create, update, upsert, and delete accept a data object. findUnique requires a unique field. select and include control the returned shape. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Prisma docs.

title: interactive transactions run several writes atomically
body: await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => { ... }) starts an interactive transaction. Use the tx client for every query inside the callback so they share one database transaction; throwing rolls it back. For a known list of operations, prisma.$transaction([prisma.user.create(...), prisma.post.update(...)]) is the sequential (batch) form. Set isolationLevel when you need a stricter isolation mode. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Prisma docs.

title: defineConfig types the Vite config object
body: vite.config.ts typically export default defineConfig({ plugins: [react()], root, build: { outDir, target }, server: { port, proxy } }). defineConfig provides TypeScript hints and can receive a function ({ command, mode }) so the config can change between serve and build. ESM is the default config format. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Vite guide.

title: only VITE_ prefixed env vars are exposed to client code
body: Vite loads .env, .env.local, .env.[mode], and .env.[mode].local. Only variables prefixed with VITE_ are exposed to source as import.meta.env.VITE_*. Other keys stay on the server side of the config and must not be inlined into the client bundle. import.meta.env.MODE, BASE_URL, PROD, and DEV are always available. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Vite guide.

title: Vite plugins hook into serve, build, and HMR
body: A Vite plugin is a Rollup-compatible plugin plus Vite-specific hooks such as config, configureServer, transformIndexHtml, and handleHotUpdate. Put plugins in the plugins array of the config. Official plugins include @vitejs/plugin-react and @vitejs/plugin-vue. Plugin order matters; enforce: 'pre' | 'post' controls when a hook runs. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Vite guide.

title: requests.get sends an HTTP GET and decodes the response
body: import requests; r = requests.get(url, params={'q': 'x'}, timeout=10). r.status_code, r.headers, r.text, and r.json() read the result. r.raise_for_status() throws HTTPError for 4xx/5xx. Pass json= or data= on post/put to send a body, and headers= for custom headers. Always set a timeout. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Requests user guide.

title: a Session persists cookies and connection pooling
body: with requests.Session() as s: s.headers.update({'User-Agent': '...'}); s.get(url) reuses TCP connections via urllib3 and persists cookies across requests. Set s.auth, s.proxies, or s.verify on the session so every request inherits them. A session is the right default when you call an API more than once. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Requests user guide.

title: BaseModel validates and serializes typed data
body: class User(BaseModel): name: str; age: int = Field(ge=0). User(name='Ada', age=12) validates types and constraints and raises ValidationError on failure. model_dump() returns a dict; model_dump_json() returns JSON. model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid') rejects unknown fields. Use Field() for aliases, defaults, and descriptions. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Pydantic docs.

title: model_validate parses objects; model_validate_json parses strings
body: In Pydantic v2, Model.model_validate(data) validates a dict or object, and Model.model_validate_json(s) validates a JSON string. Use TypeAdapter(list[Model]).validate_python(items) for types that are not a BaseModel subclass. The v1 parse_obj / parse_raw aliases still exist for compatibility but model_validate is the v2 API. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Pydantic docs.

title: field_validator and model_validator customize checks
body: @field_validator('email') classmethod def check_email(cls, v: str) -> str: runs after type coercion for that field. @model_validator(mode='after') def check(self): can compare fields on the already-built model; mode='before' receives the raw input. Annotated[..., AfterValidator(fn)] attaches a validator without a method. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Pydantic docs.

title: app.route binds a URL to a view function
body: app = Flask(__name__); @app.route('/user/<int:id>') def user(id): return ... registers a view. Variable rules support string, int, float, path, and uuid converters. methods=['POST'] allows other verbs. request.args, request.form, request.get_json(), and request.files read the incoming request. jsonify() or a string becomes the response. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Flask docs.

title: Blueprints split an app into reusable route groups
body: bp = Blueprint('auth', __name__, url_prefix='/auth') then @bp.route('/login') defines routes that stay unregistered until app.register_blueprint(bp). Blueprints can have their own templates, static folders, and error handlers. They are the usual way to split a Flask project into packages. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Flask docs.

title: jsonb stores JSON in a decomposed binary form
body: PostgreSQL jsonb is a binary JSON type that supports indexing and operators: doc -> 'key' returns JSON, doc ->> 'key' returns text, and doc @> '{"a": 1}'::jsonb tests containment. GIN indexes on jsonb_path_ops or jsonb_ops speed containment queries. jsonb_set, jsonb_build_object, and jsonb_array_elements are common helpers. Prefer jsonb over json when you will query inside the document. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the PostgreSQL docs.

title: WITH clauses define common table expressions
body: WITH regional AS (SELECT ... FROM sales GROUP BY region) SELECT * FROM regional WHERE total > 1000 names a subquery you can reference later in the same statement. WITH RECURSIVE walks a tree or graph. INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE can appear in a CTE and return rows to the main statement. MATERIALIZED / NOT MATERIALIZED controls whether the CTE is computed once. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the PostgreSQL docs.

title: B-tree is the default index; GIN and GiST cover other types
body: CREATE INDEX ON table (col) builds a B-tree, which is the right default for equality and range comparisons. Use UNIQUE, INCLUDE (covering columns), and partial indexes (WHERE ...) when they shrink the index. GIN is typical for jsonb, arrays, and full-text; GiST for geometric and range types; BRIN for very large append-mostly tables. EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows whether a query uses an index. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the PostgreSQL docs.

title: FROM, RUN, COPY, and CMD are the core Dockerfile instructions
body: A Dockerfile starts with FROM <image> and then layers RUN (execute a command), COPY or ADD (add files), WORKDIR, ENV, EXPOSE, USER, ENTRYPOINT, and CMD. Each RUN creates a layer, so combine related commands and put frequently changing COPY steps later to improve cache hits. CMD is the default command; ENTRYPOINT is the executable. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Docker docs.

title: Multi-stage builds copy artifacts from a builder image
body: A multi-stage Dockerfile uses several FROM lines, optionally named with AS builder. Later stages can COPY --from=builder /app/bin /usr/local/bin so compilers, caches, and dev dependencies never land in the final image. You can also COPY --from=anotherimage or --from=0 (the first stage). This is the usual way to ship a small runtime image. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Docker docs.

title: Compose YAML defines services, networks, and volumes
body: A compose.yaml file lists services under services:, each with an image or build context, ports, environment, volumes, and depends_on. docker compose up starts the project; down stops and removes it. Named volumes persist data; networks isolate service DNS (the service name is the hostname). Use profiles and multiple compose files to vary environments. This is a short excerpt for agents, not a substitute for the Docker docs.

title: PaymentIntents create and confirm a payment
body: Stripe's Payment Intents API collects a payment in two steps: create a PaymentIntent on your server, then confirm it. POST /v1/payment_intents with amount (in the smallest currency unit) and currency. Setting confirm=true creates and confirms in one call and accepts the Confirm API parameters. Reuse one PaymentIntent for a cart or checkout session instead of creating a new one after an interruption. Pass the client_secret to the client; do not send the whole PaymentIntent object or secret keys to the browser. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Idempotency-Key makes Stripe POSTs safely retryable
body: Stripe v1 POST requests accept an Idempotency-Key so a retried create or update does not run twice. Generate a unique key (a v4 UUID is recommended), at most 255 characters, and avoid putting emails or other personal data in the key. Stripe stores the first response for that key; later retries with the same key and the same parameters return the saved result, including 500s. If the parameters differ, the request errors. Keys can be pruned after 24 hours. Do not send idempotency keys on GET or DELETE. Use a key derived from the cart or session id when creating a PaymentIntent so a checkout retry cannot open a second intent. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Verify Stripe webhooks with Stripe-Signature
body: Stripe delivers events to your HTTPS webhook endpoint as a JSON POST. Verify each event before acting: check the Stripe-Signature header with the raw request body and the endpoint's whsec_ signing secret, preferably through an official Stripe library. Do not parse the body into JSON before verification, or the signature will not match. Return a 2xx quickly, then do slower fulfillment work. Events can arrive more than once; record processed event ids and ignore duplicates. Unsigned or failed signatures must be rejected so attackers cannot fake a successful payment. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Fulfill orders on payment_intent.succeeded
body: Fulfill goods or services from the payment_intent.succeeded webhook, not from client-side success callbacks. A customer can close the tab after paying and before your frontend runs. Listen for payment_intent.succeeded to fulfill and payment_intent.payment_failed to ask for another method. A PaymentIntent can have more than one Charge if the customer retried. Polling the PaymentIntent can hit rate limits and is less reliable than webhooks. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Responses API is recommended for new OpenAI projects
body: OpenAI recommends the Responses API (POST /v1/responses) for new projects. Chat Completions remains supported. Responses uses input and output arrays of typed Items instead of a messages array; a message is one Item type, alongside function_call, function_call_output, and reasoning. You get one generation (there is no n/choices parameter). When you only need the final text, SDKs expose an output_text helper. To disable stored responses, set store: false. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Structured Outputs bind the model to a JSON Schema
body: Structured Outputs constrains completed, non-refusal model output to a JSON Schema you supply. Prefer json_schema over the older json_object mode, which only guarantees valid JSON, not schema adherence. In the Responses API, pass the schema with text.format. In Chat Completions, pass response_format with type json_schema and a json_schema object (set strict to true). You still must handle refusals, incomplete responses, and API errors, and enforce business rules the schema does not express. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Chain Responses with previous_response_id
body: Unlike Chat Completions, where your app must resend the full messages array each turn, the Responses API can carry conversation state for you. Pass previous_response_id to chain the next turn onto a stored response, or use the Conversations API for a longer-lived thread. Set store: false if you do not want responses stored. System or developer guidance can go in a developer input item or in the top-level instructions field for a single turn. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Responses function calls are typed Items with call_id
body: On the Responses API, a model tool call arrives as a function_call output Item, not as a Chat Completions message with tool_calls. After your app runs the tool, send a function_call_output input Item linked to that call with the same call_id. Keep Items separate rather than gluing tool calls and text into one message object. Function configuration also differs from Chat Completions; follow the function-calling guide when migrating. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: create_agent is the LangChain agent harness
body: In current LangChain, create_agent (from langchain.agents) is the standard way to build an agent. An agent is a model calling tools in a loop; the harness is the prompt, tools, and middleware around that loop. Pass a model (a chat model instance or a string such as openai:gpt-4.1), an optional tools list, and an optional system_prompt. The returned object is a compiled graph. Invoke it with a messages dict: agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}]}). This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: create_agent loops tools until the model stops calling them
body: create_agent builds a graph that sends the message list (after applying system_prompt) to the model. If the AIMessage contains tool_calls, the tools node runs those tools and appends ToolMessage results, then the model is called again. The loop stops when the model returns no tool_calls, and the graph returns the full message list. If tools is None or empty, the graph is a single model node with no tool loop. You can also pass response_format for structured output and checkpointer for state. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: ChatOpenAI lives in langchain-openai
body: The OpenAI chat integration is langchain_openai.ChatOpenAI, installed with pip install -U langchain-openai. Construct it with model (and optional api_key, base_url, temperature, timeout, max_retries). You can pass that instance into create_agent, or skip the class and pass a model string such as openai:gpt-4.1. ChatOpenAI can point at an OpenAI-compatible base_url, but it only follows official OpenAI API shapes; non-standard fields from third-party providers are not preserved, so use a provider-specific package when you need those features. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: create_agent accepts a provider:model string
body: The model argument to create_agent can be a string identifier such as openai:gpt-4.1 or a BaseChatModel instance. String identifiers are resolved through LangChain's model initialization helpers (see init_chat_model). This lets you swap providers without constructing a vendor class first. Tools may be BaseTool objects, plain Python callables, or dicts. Keep the system prompt in system_prompt rather than prepending a SystemMessage yourself unless you already have one. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 uses per-service clients
body: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 is modular. Install and import only the service client you need, for example import { S3Client, ListBucketsCommand } from "@aws-sdk/client-s3". Create a client with new S3Client({ region: "us-east-1" }) and call await client.send(new ListBucketsCommand({})). This replaces the v2 pattern of new AWS.S3().listBuckets(). Each command is a class; pass input as the constructor argument. Clients are the public surface; do not expect a single aws-sdk package to include every service. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: fromIni loads shared AWS credentials in SDK v3
body: In AWS SDK for JavaScript v3, load shared-file credentials with fromIni from @aws-sdk/credential-providers (Apache-2.0). import { fromIni } from "@aws-sdk/credential-providers" and pass credentials: fromIni() to the client. It reads ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.aws/config (or AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE). Optional arguments include profile, filepath, and configFilepath. If the client is constructed with profile, fromIni inherits that profile unless you override it. fromIni is not available in browsers. Prefer the default provider chain when running on AWS with instance or task roles. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: v3 clients send Command objects, not callback methods
body: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 clients expose send(command) and return promises. There is no callback-style service.method(params, cb) on the v3 client. Import the command for the API you want (GetObjectCommand, PutObjectCommand, ListBucketsCommand) from the same client package, construct it with the input shape, and await client.send(command). Mid-stack errors are thrown as exceptions. Configure retries and region on the client, not on each command, unless you pass a specific override. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: boto3.client and Session create service clients
body: In boto3, boto3.client("s3", region_name="us-east-1") returns a low-level service client. boto3.Session(profile_name="my-profile", region_name="us-west-2") stores credentials and region so you can call session.client("s3") or session.resource("s3") with the same config. session.client(service_name) is the usual starting point for a named AWS API. Pass endpoint_url only when you need a custom endpoint. Do not hard-code access keys in source; let the session load the environment or the shared credentials file. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: boto3 loads credentials from the standard AWS chain
body: boto3 and botocore resolve credentials in a chain: parameters you pass to Session or client, then environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and AWS_SESSION_TOKEN when present), then the shared credentials and config files, then IAM roles for Amazon EC2 or container credentials. You can pass aws_access_key_id and aws_secret_access_key into client() or Session() for temporary or externally sourced keys, including an aws_session_token from STS. Official docs warn against hard-coding keys. Prefer a named profile or a runtime role. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Use a boto3 Session to select a profile and region
body: boto3.session.Session accepts profile_name, region_name, and optional explicit keys or a session token. If profile_name is omitted, the default profile is used. Create clients from the session so they share that profile and region: session = boto3.Session(profile_name="my-profile", region_name="us-east-1"); s3 = session.client("s3"). available_profiles lists profiles the session can see. A region passed directly to client() overrides the session default for that client only. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: x402 v2 uses PAYMENT-REQUIRED, PAYMENT-SIGNATURE, and PAYMENT-RESPONSE headers
body: In x402 v2 a server answers an unpaid request with HTTP 402 and a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header holding a base64-encoded PaymentRequired object (accepted schemes, price, network, payTo). The client retries with a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header holding a base64-encoded PaymentPayload. After settlement the server returns a PAYMENT-RESPONSE header with a base64-encoded SettlementResponse, whether settlement succeeded or failed. All three header values are base64 JSON. The exact and upto schemes usually settle in the same round trip; batch-settlement redeems later. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Pay x402 endpoints from Node with @x402/fetch and a Solana signer
body: Install @x402/fetch plus @x402/svm (and @x402/evm for Base). Create a signer with createKeyPairSignerFromBytes from @solana/kit using a 64-byte secret key loaded from the environment, then: const client = new x402Client(); client.register("solana:*", new ExactSvmScheme(svmSigner)); const fetchWithPayment = wrapFetchWithPayment(fetch, client). x402Client comes from @x402/core/client and ExactSvmScheme from @x402/svm/exact/client. fetchWithPayment handles the 402, signs, and retries. new x402HTTPClient(client).processResponse(res) reports paymentStatus (settled or settle_failed). By default the client only pays USD-pegged assets such as USDC and caps each payment at $1. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Protect an Express route with x402 v2 paymentMiddleware
body: Install @x402/express, @x402/core, and the mechanism packages you accept (@x402/evm, @x402/svm). Build new HTTPFacilitatorClient({ url }) from @x402/core/server, then app.use(paymentMiddleware({ "GET /weather": { accepts: [{ scheme: "exact", price: "$0.001", network: "solana:EtWTRABZaYq6iMfeYKouRu166VU2xqa1", payTo: svmAddress }], description, mimeType: "application/json" } }, new x402ResourceServer(facilitatorClient).register("solana:EtWTRABZaYq6iMfeYKouRu166VU2xqa1", new ExactSvmScheme()))). ExactSvmScheme here is imported from @x402/svm/exact/server. Hono, Next.js (paymentProxy or withX402), and Fastify packages follow the same shape. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: x402 v2 network ids (CAIP-2) and mainnet facilitators
body: x402 v2 names networks in CAIP-2 form: Base mainnet eip155:8453, Base Sepolia eip155:84532, Solana mainnet solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp, Solana devnet solana:EtWTRABZaYq6iMfeYKouRu166VU2xqa1. The x402.org facilitator (https://x402.org/facilitator) is for testnets only; do not use it for mainnet routes. For mainnet, point HTTPFacilitatorClient at a production facilitator such as the Coinbase CDP URL or PayAI (https://facilitator.payai.network), switch the network ids, and use a real mainnet payTo address. Test with small amounts first. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Pay x402 endpoints from Python with x402HttpxClient
body: Install pip install "x402[httpx]" and add "x402[svm]" for Solana. Create client = x402Client() (from x402), register a scheme such as register_exact_svm_client(client, KeypairSigner.from_base58(os.getenv("SVM_PRIVATE_KEY"))) from x402.mechanisms.svm, or register_exact_evm_client with an EthAccountSigner for EVM. Then async with x402HttpxClient(client) as http: response = await http.get(url). The client handles the 402 challenge and retry. x402HTTPClient(client).get_payment_settle_response(lambda name: response.headers.get(name)) decodes the settlement header. A requests-based client exists for sync code via "x402[requests]". This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Create a Solana Kit client with RPC, signer, and program plugins
body: Kit is the JavaScript SDK for Solana apps on Node, web, and React Native. Install @solana/kit with @solana/kit-plugin-rpc and @solana/kit-plugin-signer, plus program plugins like @solana-program/system and @solana-program/token. Build a client by chaining plugins: await createClient().use(signerFromFile("~/.config/solana/id.json")).use(solanaMainnetRpc({ rpcUrl: "https://api.mainnet.solana.com" })).use(systemProgram()).use(tokenProgram()). The client then exposes client.rpc.getBalance(address).send(), client.system.instructions.transferSol(...), client.token.accounts.mint.fetch(address), and client.sendTransaction(instructions). A no-client mode imports only the functions you need for maximum tree-shaking. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Solana Kit RPC calls return a request you must .send()
body: In @solana/kit, createSolanaRpc(url) returns an RPC object and createSolanaRpcSubscriptions(wsUrl) a subscriptions object. Cluster helpers like devnet(url) brand the URL for a cluster. Addresses are branded strings made with address("...base58..."), and SOL amounts use lamports(10_000_000n) bigints. Each RPC method builds a request that runs only when you call .send(), for example await rpc.getBalance(address("...")).send(). airdropFactory({ rpc, rpcSubscriptions }) returns an airdrop function that works only on test clusters. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Send and confirm a transaction with sendAndConfirmTransactionFactory
body: sendAndConfirmTransactionFactory({ rpc, rpcSubscriptions }) from @solana/kit returns a function that sends a blockhash-based transaction and waits for confirmation: await sendAndConfirmTransaction(transaction, { commitment: "confirmed" }). Catch expiry with isSolanaError(e, SOLANA_ERROR__BLOCK_HEIGHT_EXCEEDED), which means the blockhash expired. Use sendAndConfirmDurableNonceTransactionFactory for nonce-based transactions and sendTransactionWithoutConfirmingFactory when you do not want to wait. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Estimate and set a compute unit limit in Solana Kit
body: Without an explicit compute unit limit, validators assume 200K CU per instruction, and tight limits make inclusion more likely. In @solana/kit, estimateComputeUnitLimitFactory({ rpc }) returns an estimator that simulates the message (temporarily at the 1,400,000 max) and returns units consumed; apply it with setTransactionMessageComputeUnitLimit(estimate, message). estimateAndSetComputeUnitLimitFactory(estimator) sets it in one step and leaves explicit limits unchanged; pair it with fillTransactionMessageProvisoryComputeUnitLimit to reserve space during construction. Estimates can be off, so consider adding a margin. For unsigned transactions headed to a wallet, the wallet may set the limit. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: @solana/web3.js v3 keeps the class API but is rebuilt on Solana Kit
body: @solana/web3.js v3 (latest on npm) keeps the familiar class-based API (Connection, PublicKey, Keypair, Transaction), updates it for current RPC methods, and rebuilds internals on Solana Kit. v1.x lives on the maintenance/v1.x branch and gets critical fixes only. v3 has breaking changes: async Keypair and signing flows, bigint amounts, Uint8Array instead of Buffer, readonly RPC results, and removed APIs. The maintainers ask agents not to downgrade to v1 and to read the v1-to-v3 migration guide first. Node 20.18.0 or newer is supported. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: web3.js v3: Keypair, PDA, and signing calls are async
body: In @solana/web3.js v3 the Keypair constructor is no longer public. Use await Keypair.generate(), await Keypair.fromSecretKey(bytes), or await Keypair.fromSeed(seed). PDA helpers are async too: await PublicKey.findProgramAddress(...) and await PublicKey.createProgramAddress(...). Transaction signing is async: await transaction.sign(...), await transaction.partialSign(...), await versionedTransaction.sign(...). Mark callers async and move code that reads signatures or .publicKey after the awaited call. PublicKey.unique(), Account, and fee-calculator methods such as getRecentBlockhash were removed. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: web3.js v3 Connection defaults to confirmed and returns bigint numerics
body: In @solana/web3.js v3, an omitted commitment defaults to confirmed rather than finalized, so set finalized explicitly if you need it. Many RPC numeric fields (lamports, slots, block heights, epochs) are bigint, and JSON.stringify throws on raw bigint without a replacer. Account data is Uint8Array, often wrapped in Readonly with space: bigint. RPC arrays are readonly, so clone before .sort() or .push(). Since v3.1.0, Connection implements Kit client interfaces, so you can pass a Connection to Kit APIs that take a client. PublicKey implements HasAddress for @solana-program/* clients, and toBase58() returns Kit's branded Address string. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: MCP TypeScript SDK v2 splits into @modelcontextprotocol/server and /client
body: The main branch of the MCP TypeScript SDK is v2, the stable line, implementing the 2026-07-28 MCP spec. It publishes @modelcontextprotocol/server and @modelcontextprotocol/client, plus thin middleware packages @modelcontextprotocol/node, /express, /fastify, and /hono. v1 ships as @modelcontextprotocol/sdk on the v1.x branch and gets bug and security fixes for at least six months after the v2 release on 2026-07-27. Tool schemas use Standard Schema, so Zod v4, Valibot, or ArkType all work. It runs on Node.js, Bun, and Deno. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Register a tool on an McpServer with the v2 TypeScript SDK
body: With @modelcontextprotocol/server: const server = new McpServer({ name: "greeting-server", version: "1.0.0" }); server.registerTool("greet", { description: "Greet someone by name", inputSchema: z.object({ name: z.string() }) }, async ({ name }) => ({ content: [{ type: "text", text: `Hello, ${name}!` }] })). Import z from "zod/v4". For stdio, connect with new StdioServerTransport() from @modelcontextprotocol/server/stdio: await server.connect(transport). This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Serve an MCP server on Cloudflare Workers, Deno, or Bun with createMcpHandler
body: createMcpHandler(() => { const server = new McpServer(...); server.registerTool(...); return server; }) from @modelcontextprotocol/server returns a { fetch } object, so export default handler mounts it on Cloudflare Workers, Deno, or Bun. The factory runs once per request. The handler does no Host or Origin validation, so guard it against DNS rebinding with hostHeaderValidationResponse(request, [hosts]) and originValidationResponse(request, [origins]) before calling handler.fetch(request). Pass verified auth as handler.fetch(request, { authInfo }); tools read it as ctx.http.authInfo. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Connect an MCP client over Streamable HTTP with the v2 SDK
body: With @modelcontextprotocol/client: const client = new Client({ name: "my-client", version: "1.0.0" }); await client.connect(new StreamableHTTPClientTransport(new URL("https://host/mcp"))). For a local process use StdioClientTransport({ command, args }) from @modelcontextprotocol/client/stdio. For servers that predate Streamable HTTP, catch the failure and retry with SSEClientTransport on a fresh Client. After connect, getServerVersion(), getServerCapabilities(), and getInstructions() return what the server declared. Coming from v1, only the import paths moved. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: MCP Python SDK v2: FastMCP is now MCPServer
body: In MCP Python SDK v2 the high-level server class is MCPServer: from mcp.server import MCPServer; mcp = MCPServer("Demo"). The v1 import from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP is gone, not deprecated. @mcp.tool(), @mcp.resource(), and @mcp.prompt() still work, and input schemas still come from type hints. Modules under mcp.server.fastmcp.* moved to mcp.server.mcpserver.*, ctx.fastmcp became ctx.mcp_server, get_context() was removed (declare a ctx: Context parameter), and FastMCPError is now MCPServerError. pip install mcp installs 2.x. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Write and run a minimal MCP server in Python
body: Install with uv add "mcp[cli]" or pip install "mcp[cli]" (Python 3.11+); the cli extra adds the mcp command. Define tools as typed functions: @mcp.tool() def add(a: int, b: int) -> int: """Add two numbers.""" return a + b. Type hints become the JSON Schema and the docstring becomes the description. @mcp.resource("greeting://{name}") defines a templated resource. Run uv run mcp dev server.py to open the MCP Inspector, or uv run mcp run server.py --transport streamable-http to serve over HTTP. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Call an MCP server from Python with mcp.Client
body: MCP Python SDK v2 has a first-class client: from mcp import Client; async with Client("http://localhost:8000/mcp") as client: result = await client.call_tool("add", {"a": 1, "b": 2}). Then result.structured_content holds {"result": 3}. A URL means Streamable HTTP. Client can also launch a local server as a stdio subprocess or take a custom transport. v2 speaks the 2026-07-28 protocol revision, which removes the connection handshake and sessions, while staying compatible with existing clients. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Set up PhantomProvider in the Phantom Connect React SDK
body: Install @phantom/react-sdk plus @solana/web3.js or @solana/kit for Solana (viem for EVM). Wrap the app in <PhantomProvider config={{ providers: ["google", "apple", "injected"], appId, addressTypes: [AddressType.solana], authOptions: { redirectUrl } }} theme={darkTheme} appName="...">. AddressType comes from @phantom/browser-sdk. Use useModal() for open/close and usePhantom() for isConnected and user. google and apple are embedded providers that need a Phantom Portal appId and an allowlisted redirectUrl; injected (the extension) needs neither. Phantom Portal is currently not accepting new applications, though existing App IDs keep working. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Connect a wallet with the Phantom Browser SDK
body: With @phantom/browser-sdk: const sdk = new BrowserSDK({ providers: ["google", "apple", "injected"], addressTypes: [AddressType.solana], appId }); const { addresses } = await sdk.connect({ provider: "google" }). The provider passed to connect must be in the providers list. Call await sdk.isPhantomInstalled() before choosing injected, and fall back to an embedded provider if it returns false. After connecting, sdk.solana.signMessage, signTransaction, signAndSendTransaction, switchNetwork("devnet"), and publicKey are available. autoConnect defaults to true when embedded providers are used. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Phantom embedded wallets support only signAndSendTransaction
body: In the Phantom Connect React SDK, const { solana } = useSolana(); const result = await solana.signAndSendTransaction(transaction) returns result.signature. signTransaction and signAllTransactions are not supported for embedded (Google/Apple) wallets, which accept only signAndSendTransaction, and their transactions pass Phantom's simulation checks first. Embedded wallets reject pre-signed transactions. For dapp fee-payer flows, pass a presignTransaction callback that calls your backend for the co-signature, and never keep the fee-payer keypair in frontend code. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Generate text with the AI SDK and a provider/model string
body: Install ai (Node.js 22+). const { text } = await generateText({ model: "openai/<model-id>", prompt: "What is an agent?" }). A plain "provider/model" string routes through the Vercel AI Gateway by default. To call a provider directly, install its package (for example @ai-sdk/openai, @ai-sdk/anthropic, @ai-sdk/google) and pass model: anthropic("<model-id>") instead. The same call shape works across providers. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Get structured output from generateText with Output.object
body: In the AI SDK, structured data comes from generateText with an output spec: const { output } = await generateText({ model, output: Output.object({ schema: z.object({ recipe: z.object({ name: z.string(), steps: z.array(z.string()) }) }) }), prompt: "Generate a lasagna recipe." }). Import generateText and Output from "ai" and z from "zod". The typed result is on output, not text. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Build an agent with ToolLoopAgent in the AI SDK
body: new ToolLoopAgent({ model, system, tools: { ... } }) from "ai" defines an agent that calls tools in a loop. In a Next.js route, return createAgentUIStreamResponse({ agent, messages }) to stream to the UI, and type UI messages with InferAgentUIMessage<typeof agent>. On the client, useChat() from @ai-sdk/react gives messages, status, and sendMessage({ text }). Tool parts render by invocation.state, such as input-available and output-available. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Run Hono on Cloudflare Workers
body: Scaffold with npm create hono@latest my-app and pick the cloudflare-workers template. A minimal app: import { Hono } from "hono"; const app = new Hono(); app.get("/", (c) => c.text("Hello Cloudflare Workers!")); export default app. npm run dev serves on http://localhost:8787 and npm run deploy publishes with Wrangler. To add other handlers such as scheduled, export { fetch: app.fetch, scheduled: async (batch, env) => {} }. Serve static files with the Workers Static Assets setting "assets": { "directory": "public" } in wrangler.jsonc. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Hono routing: methods, path params, optional and regex params
body: Hono routes per method (app.get, post, put, delete), app.all for any method, and app.on("PURGE", "/cache", h) or app.on(["PUT", "DELETE"], "/post", h) for custom or multiple methods. Read one path param with c.req.param("name") or all with c.req.param(). Optional params use /api/animal/:type?, and regex constraints use /post/:date{[0-9]+}/:title{[a-z]+}. Group routes in a sub-app (const book = new Hono()) and mount it with app.route("/book", book). This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.

title: Validate requests in Hono with validator() and c.req.valid()
body: import { validator } from "hono/validator" and use it as middleware: validator("form", (value, c) => { if (!value.body) return c.text("Invalid!", 400); return { body: value.body } }). The handler reads the result with c.req.valid("form"). Targets are json, form, query, header, param, and cookie. For json and form the request needs a matching Content-Type header or the value is {}, which also matters in app.request() tests. Header keys must be lowercase, such as idempotency-key. This is a short original summary for agents, not a substitute for the official API reference.
